What used to be a niche corner of event trading is now a crowded field of regulated exchanges, each pitching deeper liquidity, tighter pricing and a bigger menu of football contracts than the last. Picking a home for your NFL trading comes down to what you actually want out of the app, not just the size of the sign-up offer.
 We tested the leading platforms across the metrics that decide a full season of NFL action: liquidity on game and futures markets, contract variety, fees, funding, app experience and state availability.  Kalshi: Best Overall NFL Predictions Market App
 Kalshi is the first app most NFL traders should open. It is built market-first, which means the whole interface is organized around event contracts and yes-or-no outcomes rather than a sportsbook layout dressed up with new labels. The result is the cleanest onboarding of any platform we tested, and the easiest transition for anyone coming from traditional betting.
 For the NFL specifically, Kalshi carries the most match-level liquidity of any regulated platform. It spreads volume across a large number of individual contracts, which tends to produce tighter pricing on the mainstream markets you will trade most: moneylines, spreads, totals and weekly game outcomes. It has also frequently priced team-by-team futures more sharply than the major sportsbooks. Active traders now get Kalshi Pro, a desktop trading terminal with deeper order books, live trade activity, advanced charting and faster execution.
 Funding is the other selling point. Kalshi links directly to your bank and takes nearly every standard payment method, so you can be trading in minutes with no crypto involved. The minimum deposit is $10. Sign up with the Kalshi promo code SBWIRE55, trade $25 in contracts and you get $55 in credit.
 Polymarket: Best for Liquidity and Season-Long Futures
 Polymarket is the largest among prediction market platforms in the world by volume, and that scale shows up where it matters most for NFL trading: the big season-long markets. Its Super Bowl, conference and division contracts draw enormous liquidity, so they price efficiently and move fast, and a few cents of edge on a futures position compounds across a long season. If your NFL trading is built around championship, conference and playoff markets, this is the deepest pool available.
 The app has also added Combos, a parlay-style feature that bundles multiple positions into a single trade instead of trading each contract separately. That gives it a more familiar feel for bettors used to building multi-leg tickets, while keeping the underlying contracts market-priced.
 The tradeoff is funding. Polymarket runs on crypto, funding through USDC, so there is a small learning curve if you have never held stablecoin. It is available in 49 states plus DC, excluding Nevada. Use the Polymarket invite code SBWIRE to deposit $10 and get $25 in bonus credit with no rollover, and the Polymarket promo code also skips any waitlist should there be one.
 You can also earn bonuses through the Polymarket referral code and invite friends to join.
 Underdog Predict: Best for Combo Trading
 Underdog Predict is the pick for anyone who already lives inside the Underdog app. The prediction market is built directly into the existing platform, so daily fantasy and pick'em players move into event contracts without a new download, a new login or a separate balance. That crossover is the whole appeal.
 That feature is Combo. Underdog is the only platform that lets you pair a prediction market contract with traditional fantasy player picks in a single entry, blending contract trading and pick'em into one slip. For NFL specifically, that means you can take a yes-or-no position on a game outcome and stack it with player projection picks in the same play, which is a genuinely different experience from the pure exchanges.
 The Underdog promo code offer is a 50% deposit match up to $1,000, and those prediction market picks need to be tethered in a combo play with fantasy picks.
 Novig: Best for Sharp Contract Pricing
 Novig is the pick for traders who want prediction market pricing that tracks true probability as closely as possible. Like the other platforms here, you trade yes-or-no contracts on NFL outcomes priced between 0 and 100 cents, but Novig strips out the margin that widens prices elsewhere, so a contract on your team tends to sit closer to its real implied odds. It is also the newest of the fully regulated prediction markets on this list.
 The NFL menu is deep for a sports-focused prediction market, spanning weekly game contracts, player prop markets and season-long futures on division, conference and Super Bowl outcomes. You can also exit a position before a contract settles when there is enough liquidity, rather than holding to resolution.
 Funding links to your bank and standard cards with no crypto required, and eligibility is set by physical location, live everywhere except Arizona, Michigan and Nevada, for traders 21 and up. Deposit $10 or more with Novig referral code SBWIRE and you get $50 in prediction market credit, the largest flat deposit credit on this list.
 The Novig promo code bonus is issued as five separate $10 credits, each used whole on a single contract priced 1 cent to 60 cents, with a 30-day shelf life per credit and winnings settling as withdrawable cash.
 ProphetX: Best for Peer-to-Peer Price Shopping
 ProphetX is the pick for traders who look at a posted number and immediately think they can do better. It runs a true peer-to-peer exchange, so you trade directly against other users rather than a house-set line, and in many markets you can post the price you actually want and wait for someone to take it. The bet slips use American odds and the layout borrows from a traditional sportsbook, which makes it the most familiar of the exchange-style apps.
 Its sports-first coverage makes it a natural home for weekly NFL trading, and the platform recently expanded its NFL futures menu, closing one of the gaps that previously kept it behind Kalshi and Polymarket on season-long markets. Volume still runs lower than the two market leaders, so liquidity can thin out on smaller contracts, but the ability to shop and set prices is a real edge for hands-on traders.
 Place $50 in trades with ProphetX promo code SBWIRE and you get $75 in bonus funds.
 How We Ranked the Best NFL Predictions Market Apps
 The rankings above weigh the factors that actually shape a season of NFL trading, not just headline bonuses. Liquidity came first, since thin markets mean worse pricing and harder exits. From there we looked at NFL contract variety across game markets, props and season-long futures, the size of the built-in fee or spread, how you fund the account, the quality of the mobile and desktop experience, and state availability. Welcome offers factored in last, as a tiebreaker rather than a headline.
 How NFL Markets Work on Prediction Platforms
 An NFL contract is a yes-or-no question priced between 0 and 100 cents. Buy a contract at 38 cents and you collect $1 if you are right, a 62-cent profit per contract. If you are wrong, it settles at zero. The price doubles as the implied probability, so 38 cents means the market gives that outcome a 38% chance.
 The NFL menu runs well beyond picking a game winner. Common markets include:
 Super Bowl prediction markets and conference futures, on whether a team wins it all or takes the AFC or NFC.
 Division winners, where the tightest races often price within a few points of each other.
 Make or miss the playoffs, a straight yes-or-no on a team reaching the postseason.
 Best regular-season record, a season-long futures market.
 Weekly game markets, covering moneylines, spreads and totals on every game.
 Player props, tracking passing, rushing and receiving milestones on many platforms.
 The season-long futures markets draw the heaviest volume of all, which is why liquidity on those contracts is the clearest way to separate the top apps.
 NFL Prediction Market Legality and Availability
 Prediction markets operate in a different regulatory lane than sportsbooks. The leading NFL platforms offer contracts through CFTC-regulated infrastructure, which places them under federal oversight rather than state gambling law. That framework has drawn legal challenges in several states, and availability can vary by platform and by market type. Polymarket, for example, excludes Nevada. Always confirm current state availability inside the app before you fund an account, since this area is still evolving.
 Best NFL Prediction Market Apps FAQs
 What is the best prediction market app for NFL betting?
 For most traders, Kalshi is the best overall NFL app thanks to its clean market-first design, deep match-level liquidity and bank funding with no crypto. Polymarket leads on futures liquidity, and ProphetX is best for peer-to-peer price shopping.
 Can I use more than one NFL prediction market app?
 Yes. Each platform is independent, and the welcome offers are new-user only, so you can sign up for Kalshi, Polymarket, ProphetX, Underdog and Novig and claim a bonus on each. Spreading across apps also lets you shop for the best price on a given contract.
 Do I need crypto to trade NFL markets?
 Only on Polymarket, which funds through USDC. Kalshi links directly to your bank and takes standard payment methods, and ProphetX operates as a sports-native exchange without requiring crypto.
 Are NFL prediction market apps legal in my state?
 The platforms operate under CFTC regulation rather than state gambling law, which gives them broad national access, but availability varies and is being challenged in several states. Confirm access inside each app before funding.
 How are prediction market odds different from sportsbook odds?
 Sportsbooks set odds and add a margin, so their implied probabilities sum to well above 100%. Prediction markets let traders set prices against each other, producing percentages that track true probability more closely and cost far less in built-in fees.
